names: the founding move of the method

entities.name: capacity-is-not-a-caller
entities.description: Memory stating that being able to build software is not a reason to build it; production stays pulled by three legitimate pulls rather than by capacity.

entities.name: the-keepers-evening
entities.description: Referenced memory noting there is one evening a week for the keeper's attention, used to argue that review capacity is the scarce, unmultiplied resource.

entities.name: the-evaluation-loop
entities.description: Referenced memory whose failure mode is described as production outrunning the keeper, arriving as work when the commit-to-review ratio worsens on purpose.

entities.name: 270-commits-in-nine-days lesson
entities.description: A dated lesson in the tree showing production outrunning the keeper's capacity to review it.

entities.name: mechanism-not-instructions
entities.description: Referenced memory linked to the idea that making the thing that makes software safe compounds, unlike making software itself which is linear.

entities.name: smaller-models-and-the-tree
entities.description: Referenced memory linked to the vessel pull, concerning smaller models making software safely inside the environment.

entities.name: card:work-environment-ai.md
entities.description: Card describing the vessel — the environment that lets others, future selves, or smaller models make software safely inside it.

entities.name: gestate-board-goal
entities.description: Related memory linked at the end, concerning the board's goal that gestation serves.

entities.name: sediment-versus-debt
entities.description: Related memory linked at the end, distinguishing sediment from debt as a framing for what accumulates from software production.

entities.name: the board
entities.description: The board that states the law: a because is a problem, never a fix, and 'I can' is not a because.

entities.name: seven wastes
entities.description: A framework in which overproduction is named the first and worst waste because it manufactures inventory, defects, and attention spent keeping unwanted things alive.

entities.name: overproduction
entities.description: Making things because capacity exists rather than because demand does; identified as the worst of the seven wastes.

entities.name: the keeper
entities.description: The role whose attention (review, direction) is the one resource this method never multiplied, limited to one evening a week.

entities.name: Depth over count pull
entities.description: First legitimate pull: gestate finished software to its vision — stranger test passing, instruments editable while they sound, the friend using it.

entities.name: the vessel
entities.description: Second legitimate pull: the environment that lets others, future selves, or smaller models make software safely, which compounds unlike linear software-making.

entities.name: Budgeted experiments
entities.description: Third legitimate pull: cheap, reversible, timeboxed experiments deleted without ceremony, pulled by a question rather than by capacity.

entities.name: the stranger test
entities.description: A test of whether gestated software has reached its vision, cited as part of the depth-over-count pull.

entities.name: the founding move of the method
entities.description: The refusal to run a factory at capacity even though capacity tempts its owner to do so; the founding move of the method this tree borrows from.

relations.description: The memory frames capacity-driven production as overproduction, the first and worst of the seven wastes.
Overproduction is ranked as the worst of the seven wastes because it manufactures the others.
The board states the same law: a because is a problem, never a fix, and capacity is not a caller.
The memory argues the hidden cost of software is the keeper's attention, the one resource the method never multiplied.
The keeper has only one evening a week, limiting how much software production can be sustained.
This lesson is cited as exactly the case of production outrunning the keeper.
Worsening the production-to-review ratio on purpose is the evaluation loop's failure mode arriving as work.
Depth over count is listed as the first legitimate pull for production.
Gestating finished software to its vision includes passing the stranger test.
The vessel is listed as the second legitimate pull, the environment that lets others make software safely.
The vessel is described and defined by the card work-environment-ai.md.
The vessel's compounding nature is linked to the mechanism-not-instructions memory.
The vessel's purpose of letting smaller models make software safely is linked to this memory.
Budgeted experiments are listed as the third legitimate pull, cheap and timeboxed exploration pulled by a question.

relations.target: the founding move of the method
relations.description: The memory ties its practice to the founding move of refusing to run a factory at capacity.
The memory is explicitly related to gestate-board-goal.
The memory is explicitly related to sediment-versus-debt.
